comment: Size ceilings in bytes for the built standalone bundles, enforced by
`npm run check:size -w packages/standalone`. See
`scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs` for what else that check does and why.
A key may use `*` to match one hashed path segment; each matching
script is held to the ceiling individually.
Growth is fine; silent growth is not. Raising a `maxBytes` in the same
commit that causes the growth is the point — it puts the increase in
the diff where a reviewer can ask about it. Update `observedBytes` in
the same edit so the new headroom is visible: it records the size when
`maxBytes` was chosen and is documentation only, enforced by nothing.
PROVISIONAL, and marked as such. Three entries below carry
`estimatedBytes` rather than `observedBytes`: the ceilings were chosen
for a build nobody has measured yet — the code-split layout from
#1438/#1465 now also carrying @doenet/math's inlined core. Each
estimate is the last observation of that script plus ~2.3 MiB for one
math core, with the usual headroom on top. Replace each with an
`observedBytes` from the first CI build of this merge, and retighten
`maxBytes` around it; until then these ceilings are loose and are
guarding less than they look like they are.
Budgets normally sit 7–8% above the observation.
Measure on CI, not locally, because the math core's size is not
reproducible across machines. The submodule's `build-wasm.sh` runs an
optional `wasm-opt -Oz` pass, worth ~10-15%, and skips it when binaryen
is absent. Neither `.github/actions/setup-math-wasm` nor the
devcontainer's `wasm-toolchain` feature installs binaryen, and the
GitHub runner image does not carry it — so CI reliably builds the
*larger*, unoptimized core, and a developer who happens to have
`wasm-opt` on their PATH will observe a smaller bundle than the one that
actually ships.

dist/doenet-standalone.js.note: A re-export facade: its one import is the chunks/index-*.js below, awaited through the version-pinning resolver, plus the render-global queueing stubs (scripts/pin-chunk-urls-plugin.ts). Carries no math core — it holds no math. Megabytes here mean code splitting got switched off.

dist/chunks/index-*.js.note: The eagerly-parsed payload every embed pays (the facade's static import). Carries one inlined @doenet/math core: the main-thread renderers reach for math. The editor stack, the worker, and the lazy renderers must stay out of it. The glob also catches a few small shared chunks named index-*.

dist/doenet-standalone-inline.js.note: The single-file variant for Blob/srcdoc hosts: every chunk inlined, math core included. Doubles as the total-weight ceiling for the code-split build.

dist/doenetml-worker/index.js.note: Carries one inlined math core. The Rust *document* core is not inlined here: it is served as the sibling lib_doenetml_worker_bg.wasm, which the worker fetches at run time.
